It has almost nothing to do with Republicans or Democrats and almost everything to do with basic economics. Labor-intensive, low-skill work goes to countries where labor is cheap and plentiful, like China.

It probably won't stay in China for long, assuming that it's there now. Globalization is lifting China out of poverty, and these kinds of jobs are shifting to poorer countries.

When I was a kid, Taiwan was synonymous with cheap plastic trinkets, and most athletic shoes were made in South Korea. Now Taiwan is home to Asus, HTC, and other high tech firms. Korea manufactures cars, has LG and Samsung, and is making a big push into biotechnology.

The only way to stop it is to legally restrict or artificially raise the prices of imported goods. That protects certain American jobs in the short term, but at the cost of making products more expensive for Americans, leading to loss of a greater number of jobs across the whole economy than were saved in the particular industry you were trying to help.
